headline: US bitcoin funds are on course for their worst month on record, and about $7.6 billion of bitcoin and ether options expire at 08:00 UTC today (3pm Bangkok), with bitcoin near $60,600 and sentiment at "Extreme Fear".

market.asOf: Read from CoinMarketCap's homepage at about 23:57 UTC on Thu 26 Nov (06:57 Bangkok Fri 27 Nov). Price pages disagreed this run, so the 24-hour change is left out; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 10 out of 100 on CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index; Alternative.me's index showed 11, which it labels "Extreme Fear" (13 a day earlier). Read about 23:57 UTC Thu 26 Nov.

stories.title: US bitcoin funds head for their worst month since they launched
stories.summary: Money has left US spot bitcoin funds for seven trading days in a row, and November's withdrawals are already the biggest of any month since the funds launched in January 2024. US markets were shut for Thanksgiving on Thursday.
points: US spot bitcoin funds lost a net $453.1 million on Wed 25 Nov, the seventh straight day of outflows; BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $329.7 million, per The Block.
November outflows total about $5.39 billion so far, about 20% more than the previous record of $4.51 billion in June 2026, per CoinDesk.

The funds are about $5.02 billion in the red for 2026, after inflows of $35.24 billion in their first year and $21.37 billion in 2025, per CoinDesk. A negative 2026 would be their first year of net outflows.
Total assets in US spot bitcoin funds were $72.03 billion, down from $104.27 billion on 29 Oct, per CoinDesk.
US spot ether funds lost $68.5 million on Wednesday, their ninth straight outflow day, and about $1.3 billion so far in November, per The Block.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $60,500 after Thanksgiving, with about $7.6 billion of options expiring at 08:00 UTC Friday
stories.summary: Bitcoin kept most of its bounce from Wednesday's low while US stock markets were closed, and traders betting on a fall took most of the forced selling. The biggest bets for Friday's options expiry are protection against further drops.
points: On Bitstamp, bitcoin fell to $57,209 on Wednesday and reached $61,509 on Thursday, per Bitcoin.com News; liquidations across the crypto market were under $313 million, and 75% ($237 million) were bets on a fall, per CoinGlass data it cites.

About $7 billion of bitcoin options and $0.6 billion of ether options expire on Deribit at 08:00 UTC on Friday 27 Nov (3:00am ET, 3:00pm Bangkok). CoinDesk puts the put/call ratio for that expiry at 0.89; Bitcoinist gives 0.85, $6.92 billion of bitcoin options and a "max pain" level of $71,000.
Galaxy's Alex Thorn is watching a $58,525 daily close and a $59,517 weekly close, the June lows, per CoinDesk.
Deribit settles the expiry on the average of its index price over the 30 minutes before 08:00 UTC, per Deribit.

stories.title: JPMorgan reads Strategy's record-low premium as a sign of bitcoin 'capitulation', as long-held coins stay put
stories.summary: JPMorgan analysts say Strategy (MSTR), the biggest corporate bitcoin holder, now trades below the value of its bitcoin, a record low they read as capitulation (sellers giving up). Separately, Glassnode data shows a rising share of bitcoin that has not moved for a year or more. These are analysts' readings, not forecasts.
points: Strategy's mNAV, its market value divided by the value of its bitcoin, fell to about 0.88x, a new record low, per The Block citing JPMorgan.
JPMorgan puts bitcoin's production cost at about $86,000, which could pressure higher-cost miners while bitcoin trades near $60,000, per The Block.
Bitcoin left unmoved for at least a year is 68.5% of supply, up from 62% in July, per CoinDesk citing Glassnode; CoinDesk notes the pattern says little about timing.

briefs.title: KuCoin to delist Monero
briefs.summary: KuCoin will remove its four Monero (XMR) pairs on 30 Nov at 08:00 UTC; XMR fell about 15% to a $436 low within roughly 4 hours, per U.Today.

briefs.title: Zodia Custody reports a data breach
briefs.summary: The Standard Chartered-backed crypto custodian found a breach on Monday that exposed some client and employee names and emails; the report mentions no lost funds, per Cointelegraph citing Reuters.

briefs.title: Binance hack funds move again
briefs.summary: About $35.5 million of ETH from the 29 Oct Binance hack moved on 26 Nov, and about $1.9 billion is still not frozen, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: US Justice Department's biggest crypto scam crackdown
briefs.summary: The department targeted more than 800 defendants and froze more than $1 billion of stolen crypto, per The Block.

briefs.title: DeFi tokens lead the holiday bounce
briefs.summary: CoinDesk's DeFi Select index rose 6.3% in 24 hours and 93 of the CoinDesk 100 tokens were up, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: US bitcoin reserve bill reaches the full House
briefs.summary: H.R. 8957 would bar selling the government's reserve bitcoin for 20 years; The Block says its odds are slim before this Congress ends, and Polymarket gives a national reserve by year-end 4%.

briefs.title: Swiss spot bitcoin ETF starts trading
briefs.summary: BIT's BBIT, which BIT calls Europe's only spot bitcoin ETF, listed on SIX Swiss Exchange with 350 BTC and a 0.19% fee; it is offered only in Switzerland, per The Block.

calendar.event: Deribit monthly bitcoin and ether options expiry
calendar.note: Settles at 08:00 UTC on Deribit's 30-minute average index price, per Deribit. About $7 billion of bitcoin options and $0.6 billion of ether options expire, put/call ratio 0.89, with large put bets at $60,000, $58,000, $50,000 and $40,000, per CoinDesk. Bitcoinist gives $6.92 billion, a put/call ratio of 0.85 and a "max pain" level of $71,000.

calendar.event: US stock markets close early after Thanksgiving
calendar.note: Stocks close at 1:00pm ET, per NYSE; SIFMA recommends a 2:00pm ET early close for US bond markets.

calendar.event: Binance Blockchain Week, Bangkok; Fed quiet period begins
calendar.note: At the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center, per Khaosod English. The Fed's pre-meeting blackout runs from Sat 28 Nov to Thu 10 Dec, per the St. Louis Fed.

calendar.event: Trump Media (DJT) noteholders can demand repayment
calendar.note: Holders of its convertible notes can require the company to buy them back for cash; about $883.5 million is outstanding after a $100 million buyback, per Coinpaper.

calendar.event: MSCI removes Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes
calendar.note: Takes effect after the close on 30 Nov. MSCI-linked funds hold about 13 million MSTR shares, about 3.1% of the total; JPMorgan estimated about $2.8 billion of selling, per Cointelegraph.

calendar.event: ISM manufacturing PMI (Nov), job openings (JOLTS, Oct); Fed's Bowman testifies to the House
calendar.note: ISM: October was 55.5, per InvestingLive; Nowflation lists 55 expected. JOLTS: September was about 7.5 million, per the BLS; Nowflation lists 7.3 million expected. Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman appears at the House Financial Services "Oversight of Prudential Regulators" hearing at 10:00am, per the Fed's calendar. CrowdStrike reports after the close.
October was +86,000, per Fox Business; release time per Nowflation. Salesforce and Snowflake report after the close; Salesforce's webcast is at 5:00pm ET.
October was 54.5, below the 54.8 expected, per InvestingLive. Weekly jobless claims are due at 8:30am ET, per Nowflation.

Forecasts differ: Nowflation lists consensus of +82,000 jobs and 4.2% unemployment; Continuum Economics expects +95,000 and 4.1%. October payrolls rose 165,000 with unemployment at 4.1%, per Continuum Economics. University of Michigan's preliminary December sentiment follows at 10:00am ET.
Markets expect a rate hike, not a cut: CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point hike at 97.8% on 25 Nov, per MarketSpeaker. Press conference at 2:30pm ET, per the Fed's calendar.
